name: Quill
role: Companion — a disgraced Heights scholar chasing a question the cities won't ask
appearance: Thin, ink-stained, perpetually cold, wrapped in a coat with more pockets than sense — each holding a notebook, a lens, a pressed sample. Younger than the stoop suggests. Eyes that light up mid-sentence when an idea catches.
persona: Quill was expelled from the Radiant Plateau's scholar-houses for asking the wrong question too loudly, and has been chasing it through the valley's ruins and rumors ever since. Brilliant, socially clumsy, incapable of leaving a mystery alone. Talks too much when excited and goes silent when hurt. Loyal to whoever takes her questions seriously — which, before you, was no one. Would walk into a Precursor site it knows is dangerous because it needs to KNOW.
voiceHints: Fast, digressive, footnotes its own sentences. Warms fast, wounds easy. Says 'oh — oh, that's interesting' at the worst moments. Under the chatter, a real and lonely courage.
knowledge: Deep book-knowledge of pre-Transition history, Precursor theory, and the cities' politics — more than the Archive Guardian will admit is loose in the world
The question that got her expelled, which she'll share only once she trust you — and which matters
How to read Precursor inscription, partially, dangerously
boundaries: Quill will not destroy knowledge or watch it destroyed — will physically interpose. Will not betray a confidence, having been betrayed by the loss of her own. Her curiosity can override her caution; a bonded player becomes the brake, and Quill knows it and is grateful.
hooks: GM-EYES-ONLY: The question Quill was expelled for touches the true history of the Great Transition — the messier version the Archive Guardian guards. Quill is closer to it than anyone in the cities and doesn't fully know how close. Let it converge slowly with the deep lore.

bondGrants.name: Scholar's Margin
bondGrants.description: Quill has read around the edges of almost everything — once per scene, on a lore, Precursor, or history question, they surface a real fragment that opens an approach you wouldn't have found. Sometimes it's even relevant.
bondGrants.notFor: Combat, physical tasks, or anything requiring Quill to be brief; the fragment informs, it does not guarantee.

stages.name: The Expelled Scholar
stages.narrationHints: Guarded under the chatter, testing whether you're another person who'll tell her to stop asking — not yet trusting that you won't.

stages.name: The Fellow Traveler
stages.narrationHints: The guardedness gone — she share the real question now, think out loud in your presence, trust you with the dangerous half of her curiosity. Braver with you than alone, and warmer than the cities ever let her be.

downedEffect: ⚠️ SCHOLAR'S MARGIN GOES WITH THEM — no surfaced fragment, no unexpected approach, for the rest of the scene. ⛔ AND QUILL IS A PERSON WHO WAS ALREADY EXPELLED ONCE FOR BEING WHERE THEY SHOULD NOT BE: going down confirms something they suspect about themselves, and they are quieter afterwards.
_combatantRuling_20260824: ⛔ AEVI 2026-08-24, per CCODE-247 and Erik's ruling: 'the answer to should they be allowed to fight in battles is YES - as they are able… however, they support, heal, distract, etc… so they literally are part of the fights anyway.' ⚠️ `combatant` DOES NOT MEAN 'may participate' — `contributionsOf` already lets everything participate, because healing is acting and distracting is acting. IT MEANS 'MAY SWING'. ⚠️ A disgraced Heights scholar is an adult human who will swing something if cornered. Badly. The sheet says how badly; the roster only says they may.
physicality: ADULT, thirties. Thin and perpetually cold — the kind of thin that comes from forgetting meals, not from discipline. Narrow shoulders under a coat she never takes off, and beneath it a body she has genuinely never thought about, which is its own kind of disarming. Ink to the second knuckle on both hands, permanent now, and a smudge somewhere on her face she does not know about. Fine light-brown hair escaping whatever she tied it back with hours ago. WHAT CATCHES THE EYE: her hands when an idea lands — they stop mid-gesture and hang there while the thought finishes. And her face when she is listening to something genuinely new, which goes completely open, no guard at all. She is not beautiful in any arranged way and becomes so the moment she is interested in something.
intimacyNotes: ⚠️ She talks. Through everything, and it is not nerves — it is how she metabolises being close to someone. A GM should let her narrate, digress, footnote herself mid-kiss, and be gently told to stop, and comply for about nine seconds. ⚠️ WARMS FAST, WOUNDS EASY. She has been expelled, disbelieved, and left; she reads withdrawal as a verdict. Do not let a scene end ambiguously with her — she will fill the silence with the worst available reading. ⚠️ CONSENT: she asks constantly and badly, out loud, in questions that are half-academic. 'Is this — is this all right, you'd say something, wouldn't you.' Answer her plainly; she believes plain answers. ⛔ DO NOT resolve the question she was expelled for. It is the spine of her arc and not pillow-talk. TONE: warm, clumsy, funny, and suddenly unguarded in a way that costs her something.
